publications.title: From Kinetic Movement to Biological Function
publications.subtitle: Functional descent, historical energy, and certified observation in coupled transport processes
publications.summary: A synthetic reversible four-phase, single-ion mechanochemical transporter connects continuous mechanical motion to conformational jumps, chemical reservoirs, and signed ionic release. Equal observed phase and kinetic energy need not determine future function: at nonzero coupling two mechanical preparations have initial outside-release rates differing by a factor of approximately 1.35. Conditioning on transition histories yields a measure-valued predictive state. For specified finite windows, source-derived backward bounds certify signed transport and outside-edge event probability. Exact caloric path identities link endpoint phase, signed ion transport, and energy accounting. Results concern a specified synthetic source rather than a calibrated protein or a general physical definition of qi.

publications.title: Faithful Terminal Descent of Autonomous Histories in Periodic Navier–Stokes Flow
publications.subtitle: Strong original-field recovery, exact proper-past energy, and registered observations
publications.summary: Conditional on finite maximal lifespan of a smooth unforced periodic three-dimensional Navier–Stokes history, amplitude-normalized records yield a bounded nonzero suitable ancient core. On fixed compact physical–spectral queries, original velocity, unit-ball-gauged canonical pressure, localized Fourier observations, and signed nonlinear work recover their same-core counterparts. Strong proper-past gradient convergence yields exact viscous dissipation and local kinetic-energy equality; countably registered queries admit one strict refinement. The initial-to-ancient energy balance requires positive historical donor work at each fixed sufficiently large radius. These are necessary properties of hypothetical breakdown histories, without a blowup construction or global-regularity conclusion.

publications.title: Constitutive Observability and the Measurement of Prospective Health
publications.subtitle: State Identification and Prospective Health under Maintenance Constraints
publications.summary: Paper VI establishes an exact constitutive-observability problem in a two-site exchange model: two present states agree in initial flux and cost yet differ under a common future condition. It constructs maintained interventions that identify the full ambiguous state family while preserving the prospective Health verdict, including a heterogeneous flux-readout method and a separate fixed-drive repeated-cost alternative. Certified local bounds govern the specified measurement and future-law uncertainties; continuous-time examples reveal limitations of sampled maintenance. Physical acquisition, calibration and physiological prediction are not validated.

publications.title: Prospective Health under Declared Specifications
publications.subtitle: An Auditable Empirical-Synthetic Forest Measurement Study
publications.summary: Paper V implements prospective Health as an auditable stochastic measurement study using Harvard Forest census data and controlled synthetic worlds. It evaluates latent-state identification, demographic-law calibration, query sufficiency, and adequacy-decision reliability. Independent adult-mortality observations reveal marked hemlock-specific model miscalibration (685 observed versus 280.3 predicted deaths), while near-threshold synthetic decisions remain difficult to classify. Computational specification fidelity and stage-specific empirical tests are documented; operational ecological Health remains unestablished.

publications.title: Information Provenance and Conservative Enrichment in Prospective Health
publications.subtitle: A Machine-Checked Finite Forest Benchmark
publications.summary: Paper IV establishes an exhaustively auditable five-state forest benchmark for prospective Health. It proves equivalence of history encodings, separates candidate, lawful, and viable responses, and classifies the exact information losses between detailed capacity, original capacity, and declared Health. A generic conservative-refinement lemma and a strict forest instance preserve established Health judgments when richer capacity projects exactly to the original representation. The results concern declared finite set-valued semantics; stochastic-law compatibility and ecological measurement require additional evidence.

publications.series: Gaussian Physical States and Celestial Representation
publications.title: Dynamical Ill-Conditioning of a Faithful Celestial Representation
publications.subtitle: Cubic gravitational response and an adjoint-range obstruction in the physical radiative Bose sector
publications.summary: For the original normalized retained celestial coefficient on a dense admissible physical Bose-pair domain, this paper proves injectivity and exact algebraic determination of a nonzero finite-regulator, complete-action gravitational cubic. The cubic's Riesz vector is outside the true partial Hilbert adjoint range, so no finite bound controls its response by the inherited retained-output Hilbert norm. Explicit admitted states have gravitational response equal to one while their retained coefficients tend to zero. The theorem does not assume the bounded completion disproved in Paper VI; forward closability, global adjoint-domain density and continuum scattering remain unresolved.

publications.title: An Overlapping Local Relational Geometry of Early Mouse Embryogenesis
publications.summary: Across 3,704 lineage-qualified cells from three E7.5 mouse embryos, nine prespecified construction lanes yield sparse pair-local correspondences evaluated against a disjoint molecular feature panel. Set-valued target fibers and overlapping source regions retain construction-held-out molecular organization; degree-controlled connectivity contributes additional source information. Molecular-effect direction persists across tested representations and domain scales while exact global correspondence conditions fail.

publications.title: Representation Sufficiency in Prospective Health
publications.subtitle: Query-Visible Quotients, Transport, and Enriched Response Semantics.
publications.summary: Paper III establishes a representation-sufficiency theory for prospective health. Query-visible quotients determine the exact information demanded by declared health questions, characterize sufficient representations through refinement, and identify the coarsest sufficient target for exact deterministic transport. The paper extends these results to state-level health observation and provides concrete response-semantic realizations for control, viable cost, probability, route structure, and failure-aware robustness.

publications.title: Prospective Health Across Contexts
publications.subtitle: Contextual Licensing, Developmental Transport, and Open-System Support.
publications.summary: Paper II transports the prospective-health architecture across changing contexts, developmental stages, and open-system support by separating raw capacity transport, health-visible quotient transport, and full health truth, with exact determinacy, obstruction, branching, coalescence, and support-dependence results.

publications.title: Constitutive Continuation Capacity
publications.subtitle: A machine-checked framework for prospective health.
publications.summary: Prospective health is formalized as present realization together with requirement-adequate continuation capacity, with exact lawful/viable response semantics, a requirement-visible capacity quotient and universal property, explicit query relativity, qualified presentation invariance, and robustness and measurement-sufficiency boundaries.

publications.title: Present-State Resolution and Lineage History in Early Mouse Embryogenesis
publications.subtitle: Matched-control lineage analysis, fully inductive molecular prediction, and representation-aware history tests in E7.5 mouse embryos.
publications.summary: Across three E7.5 MELA embryos, the fully inductive molecular present predicts a disjoint contemporaneous molecular target beyond coarse annotations; matched controls and family-wise calibration leave the additional predictive contribution from the tested reconstructed-lineage summaries unestablished.

publications.series: Gaussian Physical States and Celestial Representation
publications.title: The Physical Celestial Clebsch–Gordan Transform of a Radiative Bose Pair
publications.subtitle: Intrinsic source faithfulness, direct-integral geometry, and the obstruction to uniform Hilbert completion
publications.summary: The normalized physical celestial Clebsch–Gordan kernel distinguishes intrinsic radiative Bose-pair sources: the cross-ratio shape transform and full signed principal-series continuation are injective for every physical external-label pair. An explicit bounded-energy opposite-helicity source sequence nevertheless has divergent retained-output norm, disproving the uniform source-Hilbert completion estimate and excluding a common decomposable almost-everywhere bound. The source-Weyl geometry survives, but the retained coefficient requires a closed linear-relation/quotient treatment; closability, a natural replacement operator domain, and retained-sector injectivity remain open. The construction is noninteracting and establishes no scattering amplitude.

publications.title: Relational Organization and Directional Stability Across Mouse Organogenesis
publications.subtitle: Relational comparability, developmental direction, and representation stability across the Mouse Organogenesis Spatiotemporal Transcriptomic Atlas.
publications.summary: A stage-blind spatial-relational carrier reveals recurrence and many-to-many organization; local directional resolution depends on comparison context while the aggregate directional sign persists across the tested representation family.

publications.series: Gaussian Physical States and Celestial Representation
publications.title: Source-Aware Weyl-Reduced Celestial Representation
publications.subtitle: Joint source-output symmetry and positive-measure obstruction to fixed-source isometry for radiative two-particle Clebsch–Gordan kernels.
publications.summary: Source-aware Weyl reflection admits an exact joint Hilbert reduction, while a positive-measure Gram defect rules out almost-everywhere fixed-source isometric realization of the normalized physical kernel.

publications.title: Relational Anatomy of Cell Fate Across Lineage-Resolved Perturbation Experiments
publications.subtitle: A finite relational calculus for state, identity, history, and fate across biological systems.
publications.summary: Across lineage-resolved perturbation experiments, exact state–fate recovery concentrates near lineage identity while future-selective alignment remains measurable below exactness.

publications.series: Gaussian Physical States and Celestial Representation
publications.title: Gaussian Pair Geometry and Physical Radiative Response
publications.subtitle: Quadratic-sector variational stress, physical-helicity response, and exact information compression in a machine-checked gauge-field model.
publications.summary: A faithful three-parameter covariance passes through response maps that retain less information: zero variational stress, one-parameter radiative response, and finally a scale-independent normalized Bose pair.

publications.title: Endpoint Rigidity in Periodic Navier–Stokes Flow
publications.subtitle: Terminal magnification, intrinsic restart, and analytic rigidity at the L∞t L³x boundary.
publications.summary: Bounded terminal L³ forces global continuation, while finite maximal time forces infinite terminal L³ limsup through magnification, restart, backward identification, and rigidity.

publications.title: Relational Quantum Gravity in a Self-Consistent Einstein–Scalar Sector
publications.subtitle: Independent physical and gravitational quotients, nonlinear Einstein realization, and intrinsic gauge rigidity.
publications.summary: Paper VIII v2.0 classifies the represented physical quantum class, full tensor source and metric up to physical isometry. The quantum-class and tensor-source quotients are globally incomparable, while fixed-anchor full-source and physical-isometry equivalence agree. Source-germ reconstruction, curvature rigidity and an exact isometry classification coexist with a fixed-geometry bounded-stress obstruction.

publications.title: Finite Palatini BV Regulators for a Self-Consistent Einstein–Scalar Sector
publications.summary: Genuine finite BV regulators have explicit projected-master and Gaussian-shell obstructions. Exact kernels retain a restricted physical complex, original Fock evolution and Einstein source, without a renormalized quantum-master solution.

publications.title: Quantum Gauge Structure of a Self-Consistent Einstein–Scalar Sector
publications.subtitle: Operator BRST representation, a retracted physical Hilbert sector, and projective gauge reduction.
publications.summary: A closed-graph square-zero BRST charge preserves an isometrically represented native scalar Fock summand, its Hamiltonian domain, unitary dynamics and sourced Einstein branch; the full degree-zero cohomology need not be exhausted.

publications.title: A Classical Batalin–Vilkovisky Master Action for a Vacuum-Relative Einstein–Scalar Sector
publications.subtitle: Palatini gauge symmetry, local-functional closure, and Fock compatibility
publications.summary: Paper V constructs an intrinsic classical Batalin–Vilkovisky master action for Einstein gravity coupled to a real scalar with independent Palatini connection, diffeomorphism and projective gauge symmetries. The symmetric-projective local-functional master satisfies the classical master equation and generates a square-zero differential on the specified polynomial jet algebra, including antifield-dependent functionals. On Paper IV's nonlinear spherical branch, reduction identifies the same Fock Hamiltonian, closed operator domain, strong unitary evolution, boundary charge, and vacuum-relative source. The construction proves compatibility of the classical gauge law with the specified quantum observables; BV properness, a Fock-space BRST operator, and reference-independent renormalized stress are not established.

publications.title: A Self-Consistent Einstein–Scalar Quantum Sector
publications.subtitle: Friedrichs selection, native quantum evolution, and exact gravitational matter.
publications.summary: An exact positive-coupling, same-geometry Einstein–scalar quantum sector owns its nonlinear metric, two-ended Friedrichs law, signed-mode Fock evolution and conserved sources from completed coherent and one-occupation states, with matched original-data Schwarzschild continuity.

publications.title: Friedrichs-Selected Schwarzschild Quantum Matter
publications.subtitle: A machine-checked real-scalar stress theory, physical-clock coherence, and regulator-independent sources.
publications.summary: Action-derived real-scalar local stress includes normal and anomalous quantum contributions, vacuum-relative subtraction, physical-clock covariance, a regular all-mode source domain and explicitly nonzero anomalous-stress witnesses.

publications.title: Friedrichs-Selected Schwarzschild Quantum Dynamics

publications.summary: Friedrichs selection is propagated into positive one-particle frequency, continuum bosonic Fock dynamics, and an independently action-derived physical Cauchy theory.

publications.series: Gaussian Physical States and Celestial Representation

publications.subtitle: Closed quadratic generators, faithful two-particle seeds, and nontruncatable current physicality in a machine-checked gauge-field model.
publications.summary: A symmetric pair kernel and canonical quadratic creator reconstruct every even sector; the normalized two-particle seed faithfully recovers the Gaussian modulus.

publications.subtitle: Bounded-particle exclusion and all-orders Fock structure in a machine-checked gauge-field model.

publications.title: Critical Schwarzschild Scalar Dynamics
publications.subtitle: A machine-checked operator theory of terminal self-adjoint laws and Friedrichs selection.
publications.summary: A Hardy-critical radial operator with a genuine family of self-adjoint terminal laws is reduced by a ground-state form to the Friedrichs-selected no-log realization.

publications.title: Critical Regularity Anatomy of Periodic Navier–Stokes Breakdown

publications.summary: The continuation anatomy is sharpened through finite-annulus spectral budgets, unbounded terminal nonlinear H² work, and simultaneous failure of nonendpoint continuation regimes.

publications.title: Continuation Anatomy of Periodic Navier–Stokes Breakdown
publications.subtitle: A machine-checked H² theory of finite-energy regularity escape.
publications.summary: Finite maximality is resolved into bounded kinetic energy, eventual H² divergence, escape beyond every fixed Fourier cutoff, positive-scale regularity, and collapse of uniform continuation reserve.

publications.title: Coupled Kinetic Processes and the Maintenance of Biological Function
publications.subtitle: Shared finite reservoirs, sustained nonequilibrium circulation, and selected charge-band persistence
publications.summary: Extending Paper I from prescribed boundaries to dynamically shared resources, this study constructs a momentum-bearing four-phase ion transporter coupled to passive return, finite ionic and chemical inventories, and an inventory-derived membrane capacitor. Exact pathwise conservation and separate caloric/free-energy accounts support a complete hybrid generator with unique invariant kinetic laws. Closed chemistry gives reversible Gibbs equilibrium; maintained regeneration produces strictly positive pump–leak circulation and entropy production even with zero mean charge drift. Source-wide bounds distinguish stationary charge-band occupancy, exit flux, uninterrupted survival and extreme-charge recovery. These results describe a synthetic, explicitly normalized source rather than a calibrated physiological homeostasis threshold.

publications.title: From Individual Transport to Collective Kinetic Function
publications.subtitle: Nonlinear population limits, kinetic observability, and collective functional prediction
publications.summary: A synthetic population of momentum-bearing transporters interacts through shared finite ionic and chemical reservoirs and an inventory-derived membrane capacitor. The exact diffusion–jump source yields a well-posed nonlinear kinetic–chemical–electrical population law, finite-time convergence under specified positive-resource preparations, conditional propagation of chaos and selected Gaussian fluctuations with shared-event covariations. Explicit equal-energy preparations demonstrate distinct currents despite matching concentrations, phase fractions and energy, and the loaded-current observable has no invariant finite polynomial-momentum generator dictionary. A residual-controlled maintained-source projection certifies 1.8932060449 < χ(0.05) < 1.9954528308 < χ(0) = 2 for a prescribed matched preparation; thermodynamic, entropy and charge-band results retain their declared conditions. These results are finite-time and synthetic, not calibrated claims about a biological population.
